title: Pictures still look bare on some myth and fact slides
note: With the split kept clear, a slide such as the cafe myth and fact (slide 6) now has no picture at all. That is the rule working, and it passes every check, but the slide looks plain next to the others.

title: Arrows that point at something almost never fit
note: An arrow now has to sit in a real gap under the headline and point down at what follows. In the 48 sample slides only one fit, because headlines sit close to their body text. Hot-flat and neon lost most of their arrows. A ring round a big number is written but no stat layout leaves room for one, so it is not used (untested in practice); a line under a headline works (2 of 12 slides in the forced run).

title: Blobs and squiggles are still decoration
note: They are now only placed on slides that have room, away from text, but they still do not mean anything. The olive blob on the 10-slide checklist and the squiggle on the cover are examples. "Fills a real gap" is a weak job.

title: A highlight longer than a line still splits
note: A highlighted phrase is kept on one line only when the whole phrase fits in 92% of the line. A longer one still wraps and gets one bar per line. Not seen in the samples.

title: The lower-case style changes quotes
note: On the real quote cards the editorial style sets the quote in lower case, so "I ever read" became "i ever read" inside a quotation. Not changed: it is the style's case setting.

title: A dark heart on a dark slide
note: On a 3-slide closing slide the picture for "love" was a brown heart on a near-black background, next to a thumbs-up and a rocket. Pictures are matched to the words, not checked against the background colour, and three in a row is busy.

title: Pick for me is tuned by me, on texts I wrote
note: Across 8 texts it picked editorial-collage 3 times, object-neon 3 times, hot-flat once and dark-quiet once, so it no longer picks one style for everything. But I wrote both the keyword lists and the 8 texts, and first-person words (I, we, our) push a text towards editorial, so any personal text will tend to get it. The one real generation (a quote card) also got editorial-collage. This is a guess about taste, not a measured one.

title: Untested
note: More than one real generation per format (only one quote card was run for real), the 10-slide and 3-slide carousels with a real writer, a highlight phrase longer than a line, the ring round a number, and every other topic. The fake-writer runs show that the page and the drawing cope with these sizes, not that a real writer makes good ones.
